subject.title: [Feature]: Session-scoped skill configuration for Gateway chat sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a public, persistent Gateway session contract for skill narrowing, and should it be designed with the adjacent per-session tool-policy work as one capability-policy surface?
rationale: The request introduces a durable, security-relevant session policy API rather than repairing a documented broken behavior. The merged internal profile provides a possible foundation but does not select the public contract, ownership boundary, or compatibility semantics.

options.title: Design one scoped capability API
options.body: Sponsor a narrow design that defines authenticated persistent session overrides for skills and coordinates the contract with session-scoped tool policy.

options.title: Keep skills at existing scopes
options.body: Retain agent and transport/channel filtering only, and document separate-agent or external-policy workarounds instead of adding session state.

options.title: Expose an extension seam first
options.body: Add only a generic, enforceable capability-policy seam if maintainers want external plugins to own entitlement policy before committing to a Gateway API.

recommendation.title: Design one scoped capability API
recommendation.body: Sponsor a narrow design that defines authenticated persistent session overrides for skills and coordinates the contract with session-scoped tool policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged scoped-capability foundation is the closest evidenced ownership path for deciding whether and how a public session contract should build on it.
